3D direction vector with x/y/z accessors. Convertible to f3d::vector3_t. Inherits bounds-checked array behavior.

Enumeration of light source types: headlight, camera-attached, or scene light. Stored as uint8_t.
Aggregate describing a light’s state, including type, position, color, direction, positional flag, intensity, and on/off switch. Provides equality comparison.

Logging utility class in namespace f3d for emitting debug/info/warn/error messages with optional coloring and configurable verbosity. It provides static, variadic convenience methods (print/debug/info/warn/error) that stream arbitrary arguments, internal helpers for formatting/dispatch, a verbosity setting, and a forwarding callback API. Construction is not intended; the class acts as a static singleton-like facility.
Strongly-typed enumeration declaring the logging verbosity levels used by f3d::log. Values control which messages are emitted: DEBUG (most verbose), INFO, WARN, ERROR, QUIET (no output).

objects.definition: using forward_fn_t = std::function<void(VerboseLevel, const std::string&)>;
objects.description: Type alias for the log forwarder callback signature used by f3d::log::forward. It receives the message level and the formatted message string. Note: This is an alias of a std::function; no ownership semantics here beyond std::function’s value semantics.

Utility class namespace-scoped in f3d providing only static helper functions for text processing, filesystem path handling, glob-to-regex conversion, environment lookup, and Windows known-folder retrieval. It also contains nested exception types, an enum for Windows known folders, and a nested string templating helper class. All construction is via default class lifetime; methods are static.
Enumeration of supported Windows known folders for utils::getKnownFolder. Used to select which system directory to query.

Exception type thrown by utils::tokenize on malformed input (e.g., unclosed quotes or trailing escape). Inherits from f3d::exception defined elsewhere. Only constructor is declared here; behavior details depend on base.
Exception type thrown by utils::globToRegex when encountering malformed glob expressions (e.g., unclosed character class or trailing escape). Inherits from f3d::exception defined elsewhere.

Small helper class to build a template from a string with {variables}, support escaping with double braces, and perform substitutions via function or map. Maintains internal fragments with a flag indicating variables. Provides str(), variables(), and hasVariable().
Exception type used by substitution functions to indicate a missing mapping, allowing the variable to remain unsubstituted. Inherits from std::out_of_range.

functions.name: f3d::log::print
functions.signature:
template <typename... Args>
static void f3d::log::print(f3d::log::VerboseLevel level, Args... args);
functions.description: Logs a message composed from the provided arguments at the specified verbose level. The arguments are concatenated using operator<< into an internal stringstream and then emitted according to the current logging configuration (verbosity, coloring, forwarding). Intended for emitting a single message built from heterogeneous pieces without manual string formatting.
requirements: Each element in Args... must be stream-insertable into std::stringstream (i.e., has an appropriate operator<<(std::ostream&, T)).
No explicit thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls may be unsafe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).
The provided level should be a valid f3d::log::VerboseLevel value.

functions.description: Logs a debug-level message composed from the provided arguments. Message visibility depends on the current verbose level (debug messages are typically shown only at DEBUG). A forwarding callback, if set, receives the message regardless of the current verbose level.
requirements: Each element in Args... must be stream-insertable into std::stringstream (i.e., has an appropriate operator<<(std::ostream&, T)).
No explicit thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls may be unsafe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

requirements: Each element in Args... must be stream-insertable into std::stringstream (i.e., has an appropriate operator<<(std::ostream&, T)).
No explicit thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls may be unsafe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

No explicit thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls may be unsafe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

No explicit thread-safety guarantees are stated; concurrent calls may be unsafe unless documented elsewhere (unknown).

functions.name: f3d::log::setUseColoring
functions.description: Enables or disables colored output for logs when applicable (e.g., console/terminal outputs). Use true to enable coloring and false to disable. Actual effect depends on the output device supporting colors.
requirements: The use parameter is a boolean toggle; no additional constraints are documented.
May be called at any time; side effects on previously emitted messages are not specified (unknown).

functions.name: f3d::log::setVerboseLevel
functions.signature: static void f3d::log::setVerboseLevel(f3d::log::VerboseLevel level, bool forceStdErr = false);
functions.description: Sets the global verbose level controlling which messages are displayed. By default, warnings and errors go to stderr, while debug and info go to stdout; if forceStdErr is true, all messages (including debug and info) are routed to stderr. This setting also controls on-screen filtering but not forwarding, which always receives messages.
requirements: level must be a valid f3d::log::VerboseLevel enumeration value.
forceStdErr is a boolean; when true, all severities are written to stderr as documented.
May be called at any time; persistence and thread-safety of the setting are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: f3d::log::getVerboseLevel
functions.description: Returns the current global verbose level used to filter displayed log messages. This does not affect whether a forward callback is invoked.
requirements: No parameters. Can be called at any time; thread-safety guarantees are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: f3d::log::forward
functions.signature:
using forward_fn_t = std::function<void(f3d::log::VerboseLevel, const std::string&)>;
static void f3d::log::forward(const f3d::log::forward_fn_t& callback);
functions.description: Registers or clears a callback to forward log messages. When set, the callback is invoked for every logged message with its level and the formatted message string, regardless of the current verbose level or filtering. Pass an empty/nullptr std::function to disable forwarding. Intended for applications to capture or reroute logs (e.g., to files or GUIs).
requirements: callback must be compatible with signature void(VerboseLevel, const std::string&).
Passing a null/empty std::function disables forwarding.
If provided, the callback should be able to handle messages from any thread and avoid throwing exceptions; actual threading behavior is not documented (unknown).
Lifetime management is presumed by value-copy of std::function; exact storage semantics are not documented (unknown).

functions.name: f3d::utils::textDistance
functions.signature: unsigned int f3d::utils::textDistance(std::string_view strA, std::string_view strB);
functions.description: Computes the Levenshtein (edit) distance between two strings. Use it for spell-checking, fuzzy matching, or typo detection. Returns the number of single-character edits required to transform strA into strB.
requirements: strA and strB may be any valid UTF-8/byte sequences representable by std::string_view.
No specific preconditions or side effects are documented.
The function does not indicate errors via exceptions or error codes in this header.

functions.name: f3d::utils::tokenize
functions.signature: std::vector<std::string> f3d::utils::tokenize(std::string_view str, bool keepComments = true);
functions.description: Tokenizes a command-line-like string using bash-like rules: splits on whitespace unless inside quotes, removes surrounding quotes, supports quotes ' " `, supports backslash-escaped spaces, quotes, and backslashes. If keepComments is true, a '#' starts a comment and the remainder is ignored (use '\#' to keep a literal '#'). Throws tokenize_exception for an unclosed quoted section or a trailing escape.
requirements: Input str can be any string; empty strings result in an empty token list.
If keepComments is true, any unescaped '#' begins a comment; to keep '#', escape it with a backslash.
To include literal quotes, spaces, or backslashes, escape them with a backslash.
Quoted sections must be properly closed; otherwise, the function throws f3d::utils::tokenize_exception.
A trailing backslash at end of input is an error and throws f3d::utils::tokenize_exception.

functions.name: f3d::utils::collapsePath
functions.signature: std::filesystem::path f3d::utils::collapsePath(const std::filesystem::path& path, const std::filesystem::path& baseDirectory = {});
functions.description: Normalizes a filesystem path: expands '~' to the user’s home directory, resolves the path to an absolute path using baseDirectory (or the current working directory if baseDirectory is empty), and removes any ".." components. Returns an empty path if the input path is empty. Implementation relies on vtksys::SystemTools::CollapseFullPath.
requirements: If path is empty, the function returns an empty path.
If path is relative, it is resolved against baseDirectory when provided, otherwise against the current working directory.
The caller should pass platform-appropriate paths; '~' expansion is performed in a cross-platform manner as described.
No exceptions or error codes are documented in this header.

functions.name: f3d::utils::globToRegex
functions.description: Converts a glob pattern to an equivalent regular expression string. Supports *, ?, character classes ([], [!], [^]), alternations in braces {a,b,c}, and '**' which can match across directories depending on pathSeparator. Throws glob_exception for unterminated character classes or alternations, or if the pattern ends with an escape.
requirements: glob must use supported globbing constructs: '*', '?', '[]', '[!...]'/'[^...]', '{a,b,c}', and '**'.
Character classes and alternations must be properly closed; otherwise, the function throws f3d::utils::glob_exception.
A glob that ends with an escape character is invalid and throws f3d::utils::glob_exception.
pathSeparator specifies the directory separator used to interpret '**' semantics; default is '/'.
Returned string is a regex pattern suitable for std::regex with appropriate flags chosen by the caller.

functions.name: f3d::utils::getEnv
functions.description: Fetches the value of an environment variable by name. Returns std::nullopt if the variable is not set.

Name formatting and case sensitivity follow the host platform’s environment conventions.

requirements: knownFolder must be one of f3d::utils::KnownFolder values: ROAMINGAPPDATA, LOCALAPPDATA, or PICTURES.
On non-Windows platforms, the function always returns std::nullopt.
No exceptions or additional error reporting are documented.

functions.name: f3d::utils::string_template::string_template
functions.description: Parses a template string with variables enclosed in single braces, e.g., "{name}". Double-braced variables like "{{name}}" are treated as literal text "{name}". Variable names that match the pattern [\w_.%:-]+ are recognized. The parsed template can later be substituted and rendered using str().
requirements: templateString may contain variables of the form {var}, where var matches the regex class [\w_.%:-]+ to be recognized as variables.
To escape a variable (emit literal braces), wrap it in double braces like {{var}}.
No exceptions are documented for construction.

functions.name: f3d::utils::string_template::substitute
functions.description: Performs variable substitution using a callable. For each variable name, calls lookup(name) and replaces it with the returned string. If lookup throws string_template::lookup_error for a variable, that variable is left untouched.
requirements: F must be callable as std::string(const std::string&), i.e., accept a variable name and return a std::string.
lookup may throw f3d::utils::utils::string_template::lookup_error to skip replacing a variable; other exceptions propagate as normal.
Returns *this to allow chaining.

functions.name: f3d::utils::string_template::str
functions.description: Returns the current string representation of the template, with substituted variables rendered and any remaining variables left in brace form, e.g., "{name}".
requirements: Can be called at any time after construction, with or without prior substitutions.
No exceptions are documented.

functions.name: f3d::utils::string_template::variables
functions.description: Lists the variable names that remain un-substituted in the template at the time of the call.
requirements: No preconditions; returns an empty vector if no variables remain.

functions.name: f3d::utils::string_template::hasVariable
functions.description: Returns true if any remaining un-substituted variable name matches the provided regex pattern.
requirements: pattern must be a valid std::regex constructed by the caller.
No preconditions; evaluates against remaining variables only.

import random
import string
from typing import List

# This generator targets arbitrary std::string inputs used by:
# - f3d::type_construction_exception(msg)
# - f3d::type_access_exception(msg)
# - f3d::utils::string_template(templateString)
# The goal is to produce interesting but valid byte buffers that often form
# meaningful string templates with variables, quotes, escapes, comments, etc.,
# while staying useful as generic messages as well.
#
# Strategy:
# - Build a corpus of structured strings that exercise string_template parsing:
#   * Variables: {name}, {a_b}, {path.to.var}, {VAR-1}, percent and colon allowed
#   * Escaped double braces: {{notavar}}, {{{weird}}}
#   * Mixed literal braces, backslashes, quotes
#   * Repeated variables, adjacent variables, variables at boundaries
#   * Nested-looking braces (should be treated as literals where appropriate)
# - Include bash-like tokenization constructs (quotes, backslashes, comments) to
#   interact with potential downstream tokenize() users in the same harness.
# - Add randomized sections with printable and non-printable bytes to ensure the
#   exceptions accept arbitrary messages.
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes.
# - Deterministic randomness via provided seed.

_PRINTABLE_SAFE = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_./:%"  # allowed in var names too
_VAR_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_._:%-"  # matches [\w_.%:-]+


def _rand_choice(rng: random.Random, seq: List[str]) -> str:
    return seq[rng.randrange(len(seq))]


def _rand_var_name(rng: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=12) -> str:
    n = rng.randint(min_len, max_len)
    # Ensure it contains only allowed variable chars
    return ''.join(rng.choice(_VAR_CHARS) for _ in range(n))


def _make_template_fragment(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Choose among various patterns
    patterns = []
    # Simple variable
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}')
    # Escaped double-brace literal
    patterns.append(lambda: '{{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}}')
    # Adjacent variables
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}')
    # Variable with dots and colons
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '.' + _rand_var_name(rng) + ':' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}')
    # Literal braces and text around
    patterns.append(lambda: 'pre{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}post')
    # Mixed escaped and real
    patterns.append(lambda: '{{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}}' + '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}')
    # Variable-like but broken to be literal (single brace only)
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + ' ')  # unclosed, literal for consumers that don't parse
    # Braces inside quotes
    patterns.append(lambda: '"{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}"')
    patterns.append(lambda: "'{" + _rand_var_name(rng) + "}'")
    # Backslash escapes around braces
    patterns.append(lambda: '\\{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '\\}')
    # Repetition
    patterns.append(lambda: ('{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}-') * rng.randint(2, 5))
    # Long variable name
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + _rand_var_name(rng, 8, 24) + '}')
    # Percent and dash heavy
    patterns.append(lambda: '{' + ''.join(rng.choice('ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789%-_.') for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12))) + '}')
    return _rand_choice(rng, patterns)()


def _make_comment_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Bash-like comment, sometimes escaped #
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        return '# comment ' + ''.join(rng.choice(_PRINTABLE_SAFE + ' ') for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 20)))
    else:
        return 'escaped\#hash ' + ''.join(rng.choice(_PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 10)))


def _make_quoted_token_line(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Build tokens using quotes/backslashes mimicking tokenize() rules
    tokens = []
    n = rng.randint(2, 6)
    for _ in range(n):
        kind = rng.random()
        if kind < 0.33:
            # double quoted with escaped quotes and spaces
            inner = 'val ' + _make_template_fragment(rng)
            inner = inner.replace('"', '\\"')
            tokens.append('"' + inner + '"')
        elif kind < 0.66:
            # single quoted
            inner = 's ' + _make_template_fragment(rng)
            inner = inner.replace("'", "\\'")
            tokens.append("'" + inner + "'")
        else:
            # backslash-escaped spaces
            raw = ''.join(rng.choice(_PRINTABLE_SAFE) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
            raw = raw.replace(' ', '\\ ')
            tokens.append(raw)
    # Occasionally append a variable at end
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        tokens.append(_make_template_fragment(rng))
    return ' '.join(tokens)


def _random_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    return bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(n))


def _assemble(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Compose multiple sections to exercise different code paths
    parts: List[bytes] = []

    # Section 1: Header line with variables and literals
    header = 'Tmpl:' + _make_template_fragment(rng) + '|' + _make_template_fragment(rng)
    parts.append(header.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    parts.append(b"\n")

    # Section 2: Quoted token line (useful as generic message too)
    qline = _make_quoted_token_line(rng)
    parts.append(qline.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    parts.append(b"\n")

    # Section 3: Comment-like line
    parts.append(_make_comment_line(rng).encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    parts.append(b"\n")

    # Section 4: A series of variables and escaped literals on one line
    seq = ''.join(_make_template_fragment(rng) for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)))
    parts.append(seq.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))
    parts.append(b"\n")

    # Section 5: Optional raw non-UTF8 bytes block separated by markers to keep template parser resilient
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        parts.append(b"BEGIN\x00BIN\x01\x02\x03")
        parts.append(_random_bytes(rng, rng.randint(8, 48)))
        parts.append(b"END\x04\x05\n")

    # Section 6: Tail with boundary variables
    tail = '{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}'
    if rng.random() < 0.5:
        tail += '{{' + _rand_var_name(rng) + '}}'
    parts.append(tail.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore'))

    blob = b''.join(parts)

    # Ensure size limit
    if len(blob) > 4096:
        blob = blob[:4096]
    return blob


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose among a few high-level templates to diversify shape
    mode = rng.randrange(3)
    if mode == 0:
        return _assemble(rng)
    elif mode == 1:
        # Focus on dense variables with minimal noise
        count = rng.randint(5, 20)
        s = ''.join(_make_template_fragment(rng) for _ in range(count))
        data = s.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore')
        return data[:4096]
    else:
        # Exception-focused: human-ish message with sprinkled variables and random bytes suffix
        msg = []
        msg.append('Error: ') if rng.random() < 0.5 else msg.append('Warning: ')
        msg.append('processing ')
        msg.append(_make_template_fragment(rng))
        if rng.random() < 0.7:
            msg.append(' failed at step ' + str(rng.randint(0, 10)))
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            msg.append(' path=')
            msg.append(_make_template_fragment(rng))
        text = ''.join(msg)
        data = text.encode('utf-8', errors='ignore') + b'\n' + _random_bytes(rng, rng.randint(0, 64))
        return data[:4096]
